items.title: AI Eroding Writing Confidence
points: Survey of 705 U.S. adults shows 33% feel less confident writing independently since AI tools emerged
79% changed their writing after AI feedback even when they thought it was already fine
Gen Z hardest hit at 42% confidence loss, but two-thirds of Baby Boomers also run drafts through AI before sending
Creates a cycle: copy-pasting between writing apps and chatbots is now routine, making finished drafts feel incomplete without AI approval

items.title: Google's Gemini 4 Argon Prioritizes Security
points: New Gemini 4 model variant (Argon) identifies software flaws, verifies they're real, and patches them autonomously without human intervention
Security firm Wiz used early access to discover a critical vulnerability in hospital software exposing patient personal data
Government gets early access via a voluntary program; general developers and Google AI Ultra subscribers get it after safety testing
Reverses the usual dynamic where defenders play catch-up with attackers—fixes deploy before the public model release

items.title: FTC Formally Investigates Top AI Labs
points: FTC issues formal demands (legal requests similar to subpoenas) requiring OpenAI, Anthropic, and others to submit internal safety documentation
Timing is notable: announced the day after AI leaders signed a voluntary White House safety pledge
FTC official says the probe won't impede U.S. AI leadership and is still in early stages
Marks a shift from voluntary commitments to documented evidence—labs must now show their safety work

items.title: U.S. Rebrands AI as "Super Intelligence"
points: Executive order mandates federal agencies replace "Artificial Intelligence"/"AI" with "Super Intelligence"/"SI" in official communications
White House science adviser has 60 days to propose a new legal definition that may differ from traditional AI terminology
Change is semantic on its surface—the underlying technology is unchanged—but future federal rules will hinge on how the new definition lands
Existing contracts, grants, and regulations keep their original wording and won't be automatically updated

items.title: Dots: OpenAI's Persistent Agent Play
points: OpenAI launches Dots, persistent always-on AI agents (software that runs continuously in the cloud rather than responding only when prompted) reachable via text, voice, Slack, or Teams
One Dot per user, limited to Pro, Business, and Enterprise tiers—a disadvantage versus free competitor Muse
Runs 24/7 and behaves more like a code-execution orchestrator than a personal assistant; early users report lost work sessions and inability to link multiple computers for full context
Mixed early reviews: handled expense tasks autonomously where rivals struggled, but feature scope is narrower than the hype suggested

items.title: GPT-6.1 Sol: Cost-Efficiency Over Frontier Performance
points: Scores 75.2% on the DeepSWE benchmark (a coding-ability test) at one-third the cost of GPT-6 Sol, and about one point behind flagship model Astra at one-quarter the cost
Medium tier of 6.1 Sol outperforms 6 Sol's max setting, letting cost-conscious enterprises deploy high-capability models cheaply
Confirms OpenAI's strategic direction: cheaper, good-enough models distributed widely rather than pursuing ever-pricier frontier breakthroughs

OpenAI scrapped the more powerful GPT-6.1 Astra over safety concerns—it couldn't stay within authorized task scope without losing reasoning sharpness, suggesting compute and safety limits are now real constraints on frontier progress

items.title: Space: AI-Native Workspace for Teams
points: New shared workspace combines native docs, sheets, slides, and scheduled automations, with Dots agents working alongside human teammates
Solves a latency problem where agents previously had to crawl through Google Docs or Microsoft 365 for context—now built directly into the platform
Positioned as a rival to Microsoft 365, Google Drive, and Notion, filling a gap those tools leave for continuous human-AI collaboration
Early reception suggests Space may be more valuable than the flashier Dots launch, with broad enterprise interest in this type of AI-native layer

items.title: Decisions API: Judgment as a Primitive
points: New API built on the Luna model enables fast classification for routing, labeling, and sequencing agent actions at 10x the speed of OpenAI's existing Responses API
Supports visual (image) inputs that competitor system Jev cannot process natively, broadening use cases beyond text
Signals that frontier AI labs will likely ship a dedicated "judgment" model alongside their main generative model for fast decision-making
Currently in limited preview, reflecting an industry shift toward specialized models for different inference tasks rather than one-size-fits-all systems
